description_full: Equity Bancshares, Inc. operates as the bank holding company for Equity Bank that provides a range of banking, mortgage banking, and financial services to individual and corporate customers. It accepts demand, savings, money market, and time deposits. The company's loan products include commercial and industrial, commercial real estate, commercial lines of credit, working capital, term, equipment and aircraft financing, acquisition, expansion and development, borrowing base, real estate construction, government guaranteed, letter of credit, and other loan products. It also provides loans for 1  4 family residential mortgages, agricultural, consumer, residential real estate mortgage, and agricultural real estate and production loans. In addition, the company offers debit and credit cards; insurance brokerage; trust and wealth management; online banking solutions, such as access to account balances, online transfers, online bill payment, and electronic delivery of customer statements; mobile banking solutions comprising remote check deposits with mobile bill pay; night depository; direct deposit; cashier's and travelers checks; letters of credit; and ITMs and ATMs. Further, it provides cash management deposit products, such as lockbox, remote deposit capture, positive pay, reverse positive pay, account reconciliation services, zero balance accounts, and sweep accounts; and banking services through telephone, mail, and personal appointments. Additionally, the company offers treasury management services, including balance reporting, transfers between accounts, wire transfer initiation, automated clearing house origination, and stop payments. It operates in Arkansas, Kansas, Missouri, and Oklahoma. Equity Bancshares, Inc. was founded in 1985 and is headquartered in Wichita, Kansas.

financial_summary: Equity Bancshares, Inc. is a small-cap financial services business with a $1.0B market cap on $210M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years and +14% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $38M in free cash flow — roughly 18 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.26× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 13.7× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 14% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
